notes: Tutorial 06 of Triton-distributed 7908e4ea (inter-node reduce-scatter): reduce_scatter_2d_op, unchanged, on a 1024 x 128 bfloat16 matrix per rank, 4 ranks, with the context built by the harness (the tutorial's own constructor fails outside node 0: internode-logical-rs06-001). one_node/* is the control under triton-dist (one node of 4 ranks); logical_nodes/* runs 2 logical nodes of 2 ranks, where every rank scatters to the other rank of its node and then sends the node's partial sum to the other node.

Uses FOUR GPUs, by the user's decision of 2026-11-13 (documents/GpuExchangeProtocol.md, section 9): make two NVLink pairs visible, the two GPUs of one pair first, then the two of the other (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=a,b,c,d with a-b one pair and c-d another), all four idle. Ranks 0 and 1 then run on the first pair and ranks 2 and 3 on the second, under both launchers; under logical_nodes/* each logical node holds one pair.
Expected if the run completes, judged on the development side only (experiments/interp_gpu/internode_logical/judge.py): both tests ok, every rank returning its 256 rows of the sum of the four inputs.

The harness passes is_intra_node=False to BarrierAllContext. The tutorial then uses NVSHMEM's global stream barrier, avoiding compare-and-swap between NVLink pairs over PCIe. With this context a successful rank reports barrier [-1, -1, 2].

Every rank prints which pairs of its visible devices report native atomic operations (a line `native atomics between visible devices`), so that the result says whether the two pairs were visible in the order pair, pair.
